thread:
support-jim: heads up — NoteMart just opened a P1. They see intermittent 5xx + huge tail timeouts on the hosted API since 09:28 UTC. Customer logs show many requests 20-60s then 500. They sent sample request headers showing X-Request-Queue-Depth frequently at 900+ :frowning:

ingest-bot: alert: gateway.queue_depth_pct=93 cluster=hosted-us-west1 service=gateway (auto-detected)

support-jim: pastes from customer (redacted):
```
curl -s -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Client-Id: notemart-frontend" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize docs"}]}'
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2025 09:31:12 GMT
x-request-queue-depth: 912
x-runtime-queue-time-ms: 22034
x-redwood-gateway: tail-drop
```

maria-oncall: looking. I can see a continuous-batcher backlog spike starting 09:25 UTC — pending_batches ~ 18 and pending_tokens climbing. KV cache hit drops at same time. P95 latencies jump accordingly.

ashwin-runtime: quick thought — this reads like queue depth hit soft-limit and sample-level batching gets starved by a few huge token requests. We recently had a change to batcher.window_ms -> 100ms for better throughput; could be increasing batch wait and queuing.

ashwin-runtime: repro script that mimics customer workload (short requests + occasional 8k-token doc):
```
# quick repro (local):
for i in {1..200}; do
  if (( i % 20 == 0 )); then
    # heavy request
    curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"'$(python -c "print('x'*8000)")'"}' https://staging.api/ > /dev/null &
  else
    curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://staging.api/ > /dev/null &
  fi
done
wait
```

zoe-sre: thanks. I queried prometheus: continuous_batcher_pending_count spikes correlate with gateway_queue_depth_pct. Also see a bunch of 504s with message "request timed out waiting for batch".

maria-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) raise queue max depth for hosted-us-west1 from 1024 -> 2048; 2) enable drop_early for tenant (NoteMart) so very long requests don't block; 3) reduce batcher.window_ms to 20ms to favor latency. Which do we want first?

kevin-prod: customer impact is high, do the least-risk change first. drop_early for the tenant sounds safe. Can we scope?

ashwin-runtime: yes, drop_early is per-tenant flag. It will early-reject requests if queue depth > threshold or if request token estimate > limit. SDKs will receive 429/503; but it prevents head-of-line blocking.

maria-oncall: applying tenant flag now: `rb-admin tenants set-flag notemart drop_early=true --region us-west1`

deploy-bot: tenant-flag-update: notemart drop_early=true applied by maria-oncall at 09:42:18 UTC (cfg v79)

ingest-bot: metric: gateway.queue_depth_pct dropped from 93 -> 60 within 30s after flag flip. p95 latency fell from ~4.8s -> ~1.5s. Some customer requests got 429s during the window.

support-jim: customer confirms fewer 5xx now but still sees occasional 30s tails. They want full remediation.

zoe-sre: those tails are likely from continuous-batcher backlog and some stuck worker processes handling huge token streams. I see a few worker pods with high thread-block for KV-cache. We'll also spin up 3 extra pool nodes in us-west1 for 15m to drain backlog.

maria-oncall: scaling up dedicated pool (hot) for hosted-default in us-west1: `infractl scale pool hosted-us-west1 +3 --temp 15m`

deploy-bot: pool-scaling: started scale job job-9421 by maria-oncall (target +3 nodes)

ingest-bot: within 90s new capacity registered, inflight queue depth eased to 35%.

ashwin-runtime: after scale and drop_early I also reduced continuous_batcher.window_ms from 100 -> 25ms for hosted-us-west1 as a short-term change to reduce batching latency. Applied as runtime patch v2025.6.11-rc3.

maria-oncall: patch applied, monitoring. p95 now ~0.9s, tail (99th) down from 18s -> 2.4s. Exceptions decreased.

kevin-prod: excellent. Customer NoteMart reports service is usable again and will evaluate whether they prefer more headroom vs early-rejects.

maria-oncall: postmortem notes / followups:
- add alert: continuous_batcher_pending_count > 10 for >1m per region (new)
- add alert: gateway.queue_depth_pct > 80% (existing threshold lowered to 75%)
- add runbook step: if queue depth > 80% -> enable tenant drop_early (scoped) + scale pool + reduce batch window
- investigate why large token requests were not being prioritized (possible scheduler starvation)

ashwin-runtime: I'll open a ticket to examine batching scheduler fairness and consider token-estimate preemption.

zoe-sre: will document the temporary runtime knobs we touched in runbook and schedule a meeting to discuss default batcher.window_ms.

support-jim: closing loop with NoteMart: offered to run a test plan and provide recommended per-tenant limits. They asked for a follow-up tomorrow at 16:00 UTC.

kevin-prod: marking incident as mitigated. Follow-ups assigned to ashwin-runtime and zoe-sre. Thanks everyone :tada:
